FACT_ID: sec14-R01 | anchor: A04
Set speed for road and traffic conditions, available visibility and the applicable limit because higher speeds require more room to maneuver or stop. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R02 | anchor: A04
Slow before a sharp curve, on a slippery surface and where water stands on the roadway. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R03 | anchor: A04
Tire grip depends on the type and condition of both the tire and road surface. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R04 | anchor: A04
Keep tires in good condition and inflate them according to the vehicle owner’s manual. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R05 | anchor: A04
Reduce speed on gravel or dirt because traction is lower than on asphalt or concrete and stopping or turning can cause skids more readily. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R06 | anchor: A04
Slow before entering a curve so braking in the curve does not create a skid. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R07 | anchor: A04
Reduce speed at the first rain, sleet or snow because wet or frozen surfaces reduce tire grip. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R08 | anchor: A04
For wet roads, the handbook’s speed-adjustment guidance is a reduction of about 10 mph. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R09 | anchor: A04
For packed snow, the handbook advises cutting speed in half. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R10 | anchor: A04
The handbook recommends snow tires or chains on snow-covered roads and a crawling speed on ice. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R11 | anchor: A04
Avoid driving on icy roads when possible, and do not assume studded tires are permitted everywhere or in every season. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R12 | anchor: A04
On cold wet days, shaded road areas can freeze first and remain icy longer. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R13 | anchor: A04
Bridges and overpasses can freeze while nearby pavement remains unfrozen because their surfaces can be colder. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R14 | anchor: A04
Ice near the freezing point can become wet and more slippery than ice at much colder temperatures. [A04]
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0123]

FACT_ID: sec14-R15 | anchor: A05
Hydroplaning occurs when tires begin riding on water instead of maintaining road contact; slowing in rain or on a wet road helps prevent it. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R16 | anchor: A05
Bald or badly worn tires can lose wet-road traction at lower speeds. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R17 | anchor: A05
If the tires seem to lose road grip, ease pressure off the accelerator. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R18 | anchor: A05
When grip is lost, keep the wheel straight and avoid stopping or turning until traction returns; if an emergency demands a turn, make it slowly. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R19 | anchor: A05
Repeatedly driving faster than traffic and passing creates additional collision opportunities. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R20 | anchor: A05
If traffic collects behind a much slower vehicle, its driver should pull aside when safe and let others pass. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R21 | anchor: A05
Use an entrance ramp to build toward traffic speed before merging. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R22 | anchor: A05
Avoid reaching the end of an entrance ramp and stopping; if waiting for a gap, slow earlier so room remains to accelerate. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R23 | anchor: A05
For an exit ramp, remain with traffic speed on the main road and slow after moving onto the ramp. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R24 | anchor: A05
When turning from a high-speed two-lane road with traffic behind, signal and use brake lights before reducing speed quickly but safely. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]

FACT_ID: sec14-R25 | anchor: A05
Identify slow vehicles early so a lane change or speed reduction can be made gradually. [A05]
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0124]
